lineage: CLIPS (1985, NASA JSC, Gary Riley): forward-chaining production-rule system with a Rete pattern matcher, later with COOL objects; the public-domain expert-system shell

license.spdx: public-domain (CLIPS is released into the public domain; see the release notes)
license.evidence: clipsrules project description; verify in the zip's docs

example.input: a .clp file asserting facts and defining rules

human_capability_summary.built_to: let domain experts encode knowledge as if-then rules over facts and have the machine chain them forward to conclusions, without writing procedural code
human_capability_summary.pressure: NASA needed portable, embeddable, verifiable expert systems in the mid-1980s when Lisp machines were expensive; Rete makes rule matching incremental
human_capability_summary.success_means: the right rules fire on the right facts, in a defensible order (salience, conflict resolution), fast enough for real-time use

known_human_problem_solved: encoding and executing expert knowledge as production rules
